verdicts.why: In the 'go together' sense, agree reports concord between parties or things without approving or disparaging either side.
The grammatical-agreement sense is a technical term that describes a relation between words and takes no attitude.
A chapter as an episode of events is a neutral unit of narration; it says nothing about how the speaker regards those events.
The ecclesiastical assembly sense is an institutional name with no judgement of the monks or canons it denotes.
A library as a room or building for books is a plain place-name; any admiration in the sentences comes from words like 'delightful', not from library itself.
The computing sense is a technical label for a collection of code and carries no attitude.
Scene as the context or setting of something is a neutral spatial term; 'distressing scenes' gets its colour from the adjective, not the noun.
A scene as a subdivision of a play is a structural unit with no evaluative load.
A situation viewed as an observable object is described, not judged; the word itself does not side for or against what is observed (the 'make a scene' sense is a different gloss).
The film-unit sense is a technical structural term without attitude.
Painted stage scenery is named plainly; nothing in the word approves or dismisses the set.
A scene as a pictorial representation of a view is a neutral art term.
A strong feeling of anxiety is an unpleasant referent named in a plain word; trouble does not add contempt or affection beyond the meaning.
An angry disturbance is a bad thing, but the word names it flatly rather than sneering at or excusing it.
To have an effect upon is a neutral causal verb; the pretentious 'affected manner' in one sentence belongs to a different sense, not this gloss.
'The living' as those still alive is a plain collective noun with no judgement of them (the benefice sense in most sentences is a different gloss).
The physics sense of a wave thrown back from a surface is purely descriptive.
Reflection as an expression of something without words describes a manifestation and does not evaluate what it manifests.
A mirror-image likeness is a neutral descriptive term.
The ability to reflect beams or rays is a physical property named without attitude.
The mathematical transformation sense is a technical term with no evaluative content.
An inclination to sympathise with or support an opinion is reported neutrally; the word names the disposition rather than praising or scorning the person who has it.
In the 'capable of X' sense, capable states that someone has what is needed to do something, good or bad ('capable of such an attempt'), so the word itself takes no side.
'Capable of' meaning 'open to, admitting of' is a neutral statement of possibility with no attitude toward the thing admitted.
To continue to exist or be in force describes persistence without approving or disapproving of what persists.
